text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's National Security Service (NSS) has launched an operation to ban from traveling abroad some 2,000 Bulgarians on suspected involvement in organised crime, a NSS officer, who declined to be named, said.
-- Bulgaria's parliament is expected to discuss today projects for a new state coat of arms. @

-- Bulgaria plans to allow its university students to draw credits at preferential terms to fund their education, Social Policy minister Ivan Neikov said. The credits will have a 10-15 year grace period.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it would cut its main interest rate to 5.42 percent simple annual from 6.12 percent, effective from Monday. @

-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to raise tobacco purchase prices by an average 25 percent in German mark denomination for this year's crop in a move to stimulate local growers, Agriculture minister Ventsislav Varbanov said.
-- Bulgaria's receipts from industrial sales fell a real 12 percent year on year in June to 1.31 trillion levs at current prices, National Statistics Institute figures showed.

-- Bulgaria's government has asked private shareholders in Bulgarian-Russian joint stock company Topenergy to transfer their shares to the state owned Bulgargas in a move to restore the country's 50 percent stake in Topenergy, deputy Prime minister Evgeni Bakardzhiev said.

-- Bulgaria's Monetary Policy Council is expected to decide by the end of the month whether the country should draw down immediately a $130 million loan extended by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) under an IMF standby agreement, Prime minister Ivan Kostov said.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet said it had replaced the chairman of the Energy Committee Georgi Stoilov with Ivan Shilyashki because of administrative restructuring of government institutions, deputy Prime minister Evgeni Bakardzhiev said.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet pledged tax preferences for companies which are recycling domestic, industrial and toxic waste, Environment Minister Evdokia Maneva said.

-- Bulgaria's government approved a bill to grant tax breaks to foreign investment projects worth over $5 million in a move to stimulate foreign investments in the country, Foreign Investments Agency executive director Ilian Vassilev said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 4145
